Research & publications

Doctoral research · Rowan University

Scene representations and RF channel prediction

I study graph machine learning models that represent 3D environments and predict radio signal behavior, bringing computer vision and wireless communication together.

My broader research interests include latent representations—VQ-VAE, VQC, discrete diffusion, and transformers—and topological and probabilistic analysis for robust, efficient, interpretable sequence recovery under perturbation.

Graph machine learningMultimodal representationsSemantic communicationRF channel prediction
M.Phil thesis · Riphah International University

A Study on Simplifying Graph Convolutional Networks

Explored matrix-based representations for graph convolutional networks, with experiments on Cora and Citeseer and simplified GCN variants.

Supervised by Dr. Muhammad Kamran Jamil · Dissertation, March 2024

Read the thesis ↗

Publications & research contributions

Journal articles, accepted presentations, and ongoing work.

01
Journal article · 2026AIMS Mathematics

Local face metric dimension: a new resolvability parameter for planar graphs

Amal S. Alali, Furqan Ahmad, Zubair Hafeez, and Refah Alotaibi.

Volume 11(5), 14253–14269 · DOI: 10.3934/math.2026585

Research focus

Introduces a graph parameter for distinguishing adjacent faces through distance representations, connecting graph metrics with planar embeddings.

↗
02
Journal article · 2026Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics

Enhanced S-box design using hybrid sinusoidal rational exponential map with optimization technique

Furqan Ahmad, Muhammad Kamran Jamil, Zubair Hafeez, Adel Fahad Alrasheedi, and Muhammad Junaid Murtaza.

Volume 486, 117633 · November 2026 issue · DOI: 10.1016/j.cam.2026.117633

Research focus

Combines a chaotic map with simulated annealing to construct and optimize substitution boxes, with validation through cryptographic metrics and RGB image encryption experiments.
